title: Classes Practice Exam
description: Review classes, __init__, methods, instances, and basic inheritance.

questions.prompt: Which keyword defines a new class?
questions.explanation: class Name: starts a class body with methods and attributes.

questions.prompt: What is __init__ used for?
options: Initialize a new instance when it is created
Convert a class to a dict only
questions.explanation: __init__ sets up instance state; it runs after the object is created.

questions.prompt: What is self in def greet(self):?
options: The instance the method is called on
The class name as a string
questions.explanation: By convention, self refers to the current object.

questions.prompt: dog = Dog() creates an instance of the Dog class.
questions.explanation: Calling the class like a function constructs a new instance.

questions.prompt: How do you set an instance attribute name inside __init__?
questions.explanation: self.attribute stores data on the instance.

questions.prompt: What is a method?
options: A function defined inside a class and called on instances
questions.explanation: Methods are functions on objects; the first parameter is typically self.

questions.prompt: class Cat(Animal): means Cat:
questions.explanation: Parentheses list base classes; subclasses inherit attributes and methods.

questions.prompt: How do you call a parent __init__ from a child class?
questions.explanation: super() reaches the parent implementation in the method resolution order.

questions.prompt: Instance attributes belong to a specific object, not shared by all instances unless defined on the class.
questions.explanation: self.x in __init__ creates per-instance data; class attributes are shared.

questions.prompt: What does p.speak() require speak to be?
options: A method on p's class (or inherited)
questions.explanation: Dot access on an instance looks up methods on the class hierarchy.

questions.prompt: What is an instance?
options: One concrete object built from a class
questions.explanation: Each call to Class() produces a separate instance with its own state.

questions.prompt: Which defines a simple class with no custom methods yet?
questions.explanation: class Box: pass is valid; you can add methods later.

questions.prompt: Why use classes instead of only functions and dicts?
options: Bundle data and behavior for related concepts
questions.explanation: Classes model entities (users, accounts) with both state and operations.

questions.prompt: A subclass can override a method from its parent class.
questions.explanation: Defining the same method name in the child replaces the parent's version for that class.

questions.prompt: What does __str__ typically customize?
questions.explanation: __str__ returns a nice string for print() and str().
The second argument sets self.y to 2.

questions.prompt: What is the class attribute used for?
options: Data or defaults shared by all instances of the class
questions.explanation: Attributes defined on the class object are shared unless shadowed on an instance.

questions.prompt: isinstance(obj, Dog) checks whether:
options: obj is an instance of Dog or a subclass
obj is the Dog class itself only
questions.explanation: isinstance respects inheritance in the class hierarchy.

questions.prompt: __init__ must always return a value explicitly with return.
questions.explanation: __init__ should return None; it initializes the already-created instance.

questions.prompt: In inheritance, method lookup generally follows:
options: The method resolution order (child before parent)
Only the parent, never the child
Builtins before everything else always for all names
questions.explanation: Python searches the class and its bases (MRO) to find a matching attribute.
